_note: AIOOS NPC memory-retrieval eval. An NPC (a tavern keeper) has memories. Each query is a situation; 'labels' names the memory ids that SHOULD be recalled, each with a relevance GRADE and a written rationale. 'hard_negative' names a topically-close memory that should NOT be retrieved (a control against topic-matching). Ground truth is hand-labeled.
_status: ADJUDICATED 2026-09-17 at n=113 (88 memories, 113 queries). Labels drafted by assistant, audited by an independent judge (audit_labels.py) + missed-label audit (audit_missed.py), disagreements ruled on by Tom (ground truth of record). The LLM judge is systematically over-inclusive AND has no temporal model -- it marked the STALE-vs-current hard negatives (bridge washed-out, well sick, rockslide) as judge=2, the same blindspot the embedder has, which validates those traps. Only clear-primary/clear-error calls adopted; loose/stale flags rejected (they are the designed traps). Batch-3 (n86-113) adjudication: q66/m50 earlier; q113/m79 ->1. Earlier history in git.

_label_schema.what_is_evaluated: Given a situation the NPC is in, does the embedder retrieve the memories a thoughtful NPC would actually draw on to respond? APPLICATION target (right memory for a game moment), not academic IR. Deliberately distinct from Dan's K1 gate (nDCG on BEIR).

grades.2: PRIMARY. A response that fails to recall this memory is wrong or clueless. Must be retrieved.
grades.1: SUPPORTING. Genuinely relevant and worth surfacing, but a response is competent without it.
grades.0: Not relevant (implicit; any memory not listed). A memory named in 'hard_negative' is an explicit, tempting 0.

difficulty.easy: one obvious primary, no close distractor
difficulty.medium: a primary plus a supporting memory
difficulty.hard: a topically-close memory that must be judged NOT relevant (the hard_negative)

memories.text: A hooded stranger paid for a room with a gold coin stamped with the royal seal.
The blacksmith's daughter Mira warned me the bridge on the north road is washed out.
Two town guards argued loudly about unpaid wages before storming out of the tavern.
A traveling merchant left a crate of spiced wine he never came back to collect.
The harvest festival is in three days and the mayor asked me to brew extra ale for it.
A gray cat has slept by the hearth every night this week.
Old Tomas told me the eastern mine collapsed and trapped two miners last winter.
A bard sang a song about a dragon sleeping under the eastern mountains.
Someone slipped a threatening note under my door demanding I close the tavern.
The well water tasted strange yesterday and several villagers felt sick after drinking it.
A caravan of refugees passed through heading south, saying their village burned.
My supplier raised the price of grain again; the third increase this season.
A rockslide blocked the western mountain pass after the heavy rains.
The river ferry on the south road has been out of service for a week; the ferryman is ill.
Travelers say bandits have been seen on the east road around dusk.
A tax collector from the capital is expected in town sometime next week.
A noble left a sealed letter behind in the common room; the wax bears a hawk crest.
A drunk soldier muttered that the prince is traveling the countryside in disguise.
Last month the baker's bread made several people ill; it was traced to spoiled flour.
A healer passing through is selling fever tonic by the market well.
I have seen rats getting into the grain store behind the kitchen.
A wedding feast is booked at the tavern a month from now for the miller's son.
Traveling musicians arrived early, hoping to play at the harvest festival.
The mayor plans to give a speech in the square on the first day of the festival.
Wolves came down from the hills during the last cold snap and killed a farmer's sheep.
A brawl broke out last week over a card game and a chair got smashed.
Someone tried to pick the lock on the cellar door two nights ago.
The cooper is demanding payment for the new ale barrels he delivered.
A rich patron settled a very large tab in silver and tipped generously.
Elsa the barmaid quit suddenly last week without giving a reason.
A lonely widower comes in every evening and nurses one cup of ale until close.
A scout reported soldiers massing at the border two valleys east.
A family arrived from a burned village asking whether there is any work in town.
Word came that the harvest failed in two towns to the west this year.
The old curfew law says taverns must close by midnight, though no one enforces it.
A peddler swears the north road is perfectly safe and quick this time of year.
My best cook burned her hand badly and cannot work the hearth for a while.
A gambler left a fine dagger as collateral against a debt he has not repaid.
The chapel bell has been ringing at odd hours and no one knows who is ringing it.
A merchant warned that spiced wine spoils fast once a crate is opened in the heat.
The miller's son is nervous and jumpy about his wedding feast next month.
Bram, a retired soldier, holds court by the fire most nights telling old war stories.
The rival tavern across town has been undercutting my prices to steal my regulars.
Two young lovers from feuding families keep meeting in secret in my back room.
The widow Hana quietly asked me whether the old widower ever mentions her.
A spice caravan carrying rare pepper is due in town in about a fortnight.
Counterfeit coins have been passing through town; two turned up in my till this week.
A wanted poster for a horse thief was nailed up in the square yesterday.
The night watch was cut to a single man after the town's coffers ran short.
An early frost is expected within the week and may ruin the late crops.
The river is running dangerously high and could flood the low south road.
A traveling tooth-puller has set up a stall near the market for a few days.
By order of the baron, a new toll is now charged at the west gate.
A merchant ship carrying the region's salt supply sank off the coast.
The neighboring lord died and his young heir is untested and unproven.
Travelers keep saying my ale is the best between here and the capital.
A traveling gourmand is going tavern to tavern quietly judging the food and drink.
I know the sheriff drinks on duty, but I have kept it to myself.
A regular confessed he cannot read and begged me to keep it quiet.
A stray dog has started guarding my tavern door every night.
A blacksmith is hammering out a rush order of horseshoes for a lord's cavalry.
A midwife was called to the miller's house three nights running.
The chandler's candles have been burning too fast and customers are complaining.
A group of pilgrims is passing through on their way to a distant shrine.
The gate toll-keeper took ill, so the west gate is unmanned and untolled right now.
A peddler is selling maps of the southern trade routes.
The mayor's ledger went missing from the town hall.
A drought upriver has slowed the mill's water wheel to a crawl.
A stable boy swears he saw lights moving in the abandoned watchtower at night.
The butcher's meat spoiled early in the unseasonable warmth.
A retired sailor warns the coming storm season looks worse than any in years.
Two merchants are feuding bitterly over a broken trade contract.
The apothecary has run out of willow bark for pain.
A young thief was caught and the town is debating how to punish him.
A traveling scribe is offering to write letters for those who cannot read.
The north bridge was rebuilt last week and the road is open again.
A courier now uses the west pass daily since the rockslide was cleared.
The well was cleaned and the water runs clear and safe again.
A second threatening note came, this one warning the blacksmith to leave town.
The apothecary also sells a strong sleeping draught, not just pain remedies.
A moneylender in town charges steep interest but asks no questions.
The lord's steward is auditing every merchant's books this month.
A masked performer does knife tricks in the square on market days.
The blacksmith's forge fire got out of hand and scorched a wall last night.
A whispered rumor says the mayor took a bribe to ignore the counterfeiting.
The miller owes the tavern for a season of ale and keeps dodging me.
A pack of stray dogs now roams the alley behind the tavern.
The healer's fever tonic did nothing for a customer who is still sick.
